samples.summary: Apply guard compares hrefs, so a caret that moved into a *different* link with the same URL passes the check and that other link is silently rewritten
samples.evidence: `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref)` only compares href *values*, not link identity. The comment two lines above states the guard exists because "the caret can also have moved into a different hyperlink, where `insertLink` would rewrite that one — a silent edit to a link the user never opened." When the document links the same URL twice (ordinary), the user can open the popover on link 1, click into link 2, press Apply: `getLinkAtCursor()` returns the identical href, the guard passes, and `insertLink` rewrites link 2 (including replacing its display text when it is URL-derived, via the new `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace`) while the link the popover was opened for stays stale. The guard needs the link's block+offset identity, not its href.

samples.summary: The Apply guard is skipped entirely for the ⌘K-over-a-selection flow, so the "caret left, Apply inserts the URL as plain text somewhere else" bug is still live there
samples.evidence: `editingHref` is set from `editRequest.initialUrl || null`, and docs-view.tsx:465 passes `editor.getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""`. When ⌘K is pressed with a selection over plain text there is no link at the caret, so `editingHref` stays `null` and the guard short-circuits. The user can then click into the body (destroying the selection and moving the caret) and press Apply: `insertLink` falls into its caret branch and inserts the URL as literal text at wherever the caret now is, instead of linking the text that was selected — the same failure mode the guard was added to prevent, just with `editingHref === null`. Nothing records "there was a selection when this popover opened".

samples.summary: Call sites re-inject the stale `lineAffinity` that `withOffset` deliberately dropped from a snapped endpoint, so the caret at the new offset carries the affinity computed for the old one
samples.evidence: `withOffset` (link-run.ts:183) returns a position *without* `lineAffinity` whenever it moves an endpoint, documented as "dropping a now-stale wrap affinity". Every new call site then writes `this.cursor.moveTo(snapped.focus, snapped.focus.lineAffinity ?? result.lineAffinity)` (text-editor.ts:2019, 2075, 2245, 2375) and `Cursor.moveTo` gives the explicit argument precedence (cursor.ts:55). So in exactly the case the drop was written for — the endpoint moved — the affinity resolved at the *un-snapped* offset is applied to the snapped offset. The stored selection endpoint has no affinity while the caret has one, so at a wrap boundary the caret can paint on a different visual line from the selection's end.

samples.summary: The text-box editor's selection branch of `insertLink` was not given the covering-link rewrite, so #1038 Part A remains for a selected self-labelled link there
samples.evidence: `initializeTextBox.insertLink` still does only `docStore.snapshot(); doc.applyInlineStyle(range, { href: url })` for a selection (text-box-editor.ts:1187-1193), while the docs editor's equivalent branch now routes an exactly-covering link through `linkRunCoveringRange` + `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` (editor.ts:3612-3631). Selecting a self-labelled link inside a text box (e.g. Ctrl+A over a block whose whole text is the URL — the flow the new `selectAll()` test helper exercises) and applying a new URL leaves the old URL as the visible text with a different href, the exact stale-label state the change fixes everywhere else.

samples.summary: The rewritten selection always points anchor→start / focus→end, flipping a backward selection and jumping the caret to the other end of the link
samples.evidence: `const rewritten = { anchor: {offset: covered.run.start}, focus: {offset: caretOffset} }` ignores the original range's direction. A user who dragged right-to-left over the link (anchor at the link end, focus at the start) has the caret jump from the left edge to the right edge after Apply. Also unlike the fresh-insert path, this branch never sets `needsScrollIntoView`, so a rewrite that lengthens the text can leave the new caret off-screen.

samples.summary: Comment asserts the opposite of the actual behaviour for multi-block header/footer ranges
samples.evidence: The new comment claims "A range spanning two header/footer blocks is left alone by `expandRangeForLinks`, whose `anchorComesFirst` declines to order what `getBlockIndex` cannot see." But `setEditContext` keeps `doc.editContext` in sync (text-editor.ts:401-404) and `Doc.getBlockIndex` indexes `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:271), which returns the *header* blocks in header context — so both endpoints resolve to non-negative indices and such a range IS ordered and snapped. The behaviour is fine; the recorded invariant is wrong and would mislead a later change that relies on it.

finding.summary: Apply guard compares hrefs, so a caret that moved into a *different* link with the same URL passes the check and that other link is silently rewritten
finding.evidence: `if (editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref)` only compares href *values*, not link identity. The comment two lines above states the guard exists because "the caret can also have moved into a different hyperlink, where `insertLink` would rewrite that one — a silent edit to a link the user never opened." When the document links the same URL twice (ordinary), the user can open the popover on link 1, click into link 2, press Apply: `getLinkAtCursor()` returns the identical href, the guard passes, and `insertLink` rewrites link 2 (including replacing its display text when it is URL-derived, via the new `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace`) while the link the popover was opened for stays stale. The guard needs the link's block+offset identity, not its href.

verdict.reason: The guard is present exactly as described and is href-value-based, not identity-based. `editingHref` only ever holds a URL string (docs-link-popover.tsx:100 from editRequest.initialUrl, :142 from linkInfo.href), and `editor.getLinkAtCursor()` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3713-3737) returns only `inline.style.href` at the caret — neither carries block id or run offsets, so two distinct link runs sharing a URL compare equal. The path is reachable in normal use: the popover intentionally stays open in edit mode when the caret leaves the link (onCursorLinkChange keeps mode==='edit', :74-88) and there is no outside-click dismissal (only scroll, :117-127). When Apply then passes the guard, `editor.insertLink(url)` (:173) acts purely on the current cursor: the caret branch at editor.ts:3644-3676 resolves the link via `findLinkRunAt(block, pos.offset)` and calls `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace`, which also rewrites URL-derived display text (comment at editor.ts:3661-3662). Result: link 2 is silently rewritten while the link the popover was opened on stays unchanged — the exact failure the guard's own comment (:53-55) says it exists to prevent. No upstream guard exists; docs-view.tsx:630-636 passes only the editor and editRequest, with no link-identity token anywhere in the flow. This is a silent wrong-target document mutation on an ordinary document, squarely in the correctness lane.
